facts.detail: Ofcom published the universal-service-obligations page on 17 March 2023.
Universal service obligations provide a safety net for requesting a minimum set of communications services at affordable prices.
BT and KCOM are the designated broadband and telephony universal service providers in the UK.
The Government introduced broadband universal-service legislation in March 2018.
Ofcom implemented the broadband universal-service conditions for BT and KCOM in March 2020.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the consumer broadband-speeds guide on 21 November 2022.
The Broadband Speeds Code requires clear information about expected speeds when a broadband service is purchased.
Estimated speeds should reflect busy periods of 8–10pm for home services and 12–2pm for business services.
Providers should supply a personalised minimum guaranteed broadband speed.
When a provider-network problem cannot be fixed within 30 days, the customer must be allowed to leave without an early-exit fee.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the checker page on 17 August 2022 and last updated it on 25 June 2025.
The checkers accept a postcode and show mobile coverage by provider plus standard, superfast and ultrafast broadband availability.
Checker results can also be viewed as interactive maps.
Ofcom makes fixed-broadband and mobile data available to developers through an API.
The coverage checker does not report local maintenance or reported network faults; users are directed to provider status information.

facts.detail: Ofcom last updated the decent-broadband consumer guide on 19 June 2026.
Every UK home and business has a legal right to request a decent, affordable broadband connection.
A decent connection is defined as at least 10 Mbit/s download and 1 Mbit/s upload.
Eligible users can request an upgraded connection from BT, or from KCOM in the Hull area.
Applicants do not need to be existing BT or KCOM customers, and fixed-wireless or satellite options may also be available.

facts.detail: The calendar records publication of the Q1 2026 Telecommunications Market Data Update on 23 July 2026.
The market-data update provides high-level fixed and mobile telecoms market-sizing statistics.
The Q1 2026 market-data release is listed with both PDF and CSV files.
The calendar also records publication of Telecoms and Pay-TV Complaints Q1 2026 on 23 July 2026.
The complaints release ranks major providers with more than 1.5% market share by complaints per 100,000 subscribers.
